facts.fact: Opened 1939; built by the CCC and WPA; on the National Register of Historic Places; the holes are named after Black pioneers of American golf.

The Wake-Robin Golf Club (1937, Helen Webb Harris) and the Royal Golf Club petitioned in 1938 to desegregate DC's public courses; Langston opened in 1939. The wake-robin is an early-spring wildflower.
The course's back tees are named Royal.

current.subject: A three-petalled orange wildflower.
current.keep: The three-petalled flower, read as the wake-robin.
current.weaknesses: Side-on with stem and leaves; not identifiable as a trillium.

concepts.name: Wake-Robin
concepts.rationale: A red trillium (wake-robin) from above: three petals over three leaves, a perfect three-fold emblem.
concepts.symbolism: The women's club whose petition helped open the course.
concepts.tradeoffs: The link is a reading of the current flower; the developer should confirm.

concepts.name: Royal Tees
concepts.rationale: A crown whose points are golf tees on a gold band, on royal purple.
concepts.symbolism: The men's club that petitioned alongside Wake-Robin.
concepts.tradeoffs: Crowns are generic; the story is needed.

recommendation: Concept 1. The trillium honours Langston's founding history and is the strongest mark.
